newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields off slightly, await US data.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields off slightly, await US data.

text.p: *Australian bonds yields stayed around their initial lows during a thinly traded morning session as the market remained cautious ahead of the first of this week's key U.S. indicators.
*Holiday in Tokyo keeps interest low key.
Australian bonds yields stayed around their initial lows during a thinly traded morning session as the market remained cautious ahead of the first of this week's key U.S. indicators.
The market met a firmer tone at the start of trading, mimicking the action in U.S. Treasuries in New York, and after Monday's local corrective sell-off was seen as overdone.
There is no trading in U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo today due to a holiday in Japan for Green Day.
The immediate focus for the market will be the release of the U.S. first employment cost index later on Tuesday.

This report, along with Wednesday's first quarter GDP and Friday's April non-farm payrolls, are seen as the decisive indicators as to whether the Federal Open Market Committee will endorse a further tightening in the Fed funds rate on May 20.

Conversely, this week's data out of Australia could stir up thoughts of a further monetary easing if they prove weak, and following last week's moderate "living wage" claim outcome and subdued inflation report, although the general view at this stage is that official rates are on hold for some time.
First quarter average weekly ordinary time earnings and building approvals are due Thursday and retail trade on Friday.

Spread differentials to the U.S. were little changed, but they narrowed sharply to Canada amid continued weakness in the Canadian dollar. The fall was partly due to jitters over the June 2 Canadian election with Prime Minister Jean Chretien saying he may reverse some planned spending cuts.
